steps.title: 3.4 · unique root in the bracket
steps.raw: $J_2(\psi+p,p,k)=0$ has exactly one solution $p_*(\psi,k)$ in $[p_0,p_1]$
steps.note: Conditional on JacobiFull and finite tangencies. This matches the scalar root count, not continuity, extrema or the geometric time conversion.

steps.title: 3.4 · no earlier root
steps.raw: and none in $(0,p_0)$
steps.note: Strict positivity excludes a zero in (0,p₀), under JacobiFull. This is a positivity counterpart of the no-root clause.

steps.title: 3.4 proof · bracket sign conditions
steps.raw:
On $(p_0,p_1)$ one has $s>0$ (as $K<p_0<p_1\le2K$), $f_1>0$ and $\beta_1<0$
by Lemma~\ref{lem:identities}(iv), and $\alpha_1>0$, since $\alpha_1(p_0)>0$
by Lemma~\ref{lem:identities}(iv) and $p_1$ is at most the first zero of
$\alpha_1$ after $p_0$; so $\beta<0<\alpha$, i.e.\ $0<y<1$; $y=1$ at $p_0$ ($\beta=0$) and $y=0$ at $p_1$ ($\alpha=0$).
steps.note: The sign fields are checked on the abstract left bracket. For the first bracket m = 0 the parity factor is 1. The y endpoint formulas require the other bracket lemmas.

steps.title: 3.4 proof · continuous lift and slope bound
steps.note: The continuous lift, its endpoint values and the oriented slope bound are checked for SBracket. Analyticity in this excerpt is outside those declarations.

steps.title: 3.4 proof · endpoint divergence
steps.raw:
and $u'\to\infty$ as $p\to p_0$, because $r(p_0)=0$
and $r'(p_0)\ne0$: at the zero $p_0$ of $f_1$, $T_1=d^2b\ne0$ in
\eqref{eq:zprime}.
steps.note: No compiled proof of this endpoint-divergence argument is indexed. Finite tangencies are an explicit assumption of the counting theorem.

steps.title: 3.4 proof · apply crossing to the first bracket
steps.raw:
Lemma~\ref{lem:crossing} on $[p_0,p_1]$, with \eqref{eq:zero-set}, gives
exactly one root there
steps.note: Conditional on JacobiFull and finite tangencies. This matches the scalar root count, not continuity, extrema or the geometric time conversion. The witness-construction and q ≥ p₀ uniqueness branches reuse this bracket count to assemble the positive-interval result.

steps.title: 3.4 proof · dependence on initial phase
steps.raw:
, continuous in $\psi$ because the branches are
strictly monotone.
steps.note: Continuity of the selected root as a function of ψ has no compiled counterpart in this snapshot.

steps.title: 3.4 proof · positivity rules out earlier roots
steps.raw:
On $(0,p_0)$, $f_1<0$ and $\beta_1<0$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:identities}(iv), so $\beta>0$ and
$\alpha=(1-k^2)(\beta+\ell)>0$: $J_2>0$, no root (this is
\cite[Theorem~2.2]{Sachkov2010Conjugate}).
steps.note: The fully applied J2_pos_before_p0 proof supplies strict positivity in the contradiction branch of first_time_complete. The bracket count still requires finite tangencies.

steps.title: 3.4 proof · corner phases, extrema and cut time
steps.raw:
The corner phases are
$\psi_\pm(p_0)=-p_0$ and $\psi_\pm(p_1)=K-p_1$, where $p_*=p_0$ and
$p_*=p_1$; every other phase is attained at an interior $p$.  The cut
time is $2kp_0$ \cite[Theorem~3.3]{Sachkov2010Conjugate}.
steps.note: The root extrema, their unique attaining phases and cut-time interpretation are not established by the scalar counting declarations.

steps.title: 4.1 · one root on each bracket and no other roots
steps.raw:
Consequently, for every initial phase, the geodesic has exactly one
conjugate time on each closed bracket and none elsewhere in
$[p_n^1,p_{n+1}^1)$.
steps.note: Lean m is article n − 1. JacobiFull and finite tangencies hL/hR remain assumptions; zero orders and identification of k₀ are not certified.

steps.title: 4.1 · distinct roots and critical coincidence
steps.raw:
The two bracket roots are distinct except when
$k=k_0$ and $\psi\equiv K\pmod{2K}$: in that case the cell contains the
single conjugate time $p=2nK$.
steps.note: Two roots are checked for K ≠ 2E; coincidence forces the even-period endpoint and K = 2E. The numerical identification of k₀ and zero order are separate, unformalized claims.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · no root after bₙ
steps.raw:
On $(b_n,p_{n+1}^1)$, $f_1$ and $\beta_1$ have the common sign
$(-1)^{n+1}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:identities}(iv), so $\beta>0$ and
$\alpha=(1-k^2)(\ell+\beta)>0$: $J_2>0$, no zero (there $y>1$).
steps.note: J2_pos_after_bR proves positivity on (bR m, pL (m+1)); m = n − 1. Its application excludes this region from the cell zero set.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · no root between the two brackets
steps.raw:
On $(p_n^1,b_n)$,
$f_1$ and $\beta_1$ have opposite signs, so $\beta<0$; $s$ has the sign
$(-1)^{n+1}$ before $2nK$ and $(-1)^n$ after, and $\alpha_1$ has the sign
$(-1)^{n+1}$ before $p_n^\alpha$ and $(-1)^n$ after
(Lemma~\ref{lem:identities}(iv)).  Hence $X=s\,\alpha_1<0$ strictly
between $2nK$ and $p_n^\alpha$, where $\beta=X-\ell<0$ and
$\alpha=(1-k^2)X<0$ give $J_2<0$: no zero (there $y<0$).
steps.note: J2_neg_gap proves strict negativity on (eL m, eR m). The indexed call is the gap-exclusion branch of cell_roots, under JacobiFull.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · oriented phase lifts on both brackets
steps.raw:
On the
two open brackets $X>0$,
so $0<y<1$, with $y=1$ at $p_n^1$ and $b_n$ ($\beta=0$) and $y=0$ at $2nK$
and $p_n^\alpha$ ($X=0$); thus $r$ runs between $0$ and $1$ and $u$ between
$0$ and $K$, from $0$ to $K$ on $B_n^-$ and from $K$ to $0$ on $B_n^+$,
with $|u'|\ge1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:riccati})
steps.note: SBracket proves continuous lift endpoints and an oriented slope bound. The left/right bracket orientations supply the two directions; this is not a proof of endpoint blow-up or analyticity.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · endpoint regularity and critical continuation
steps.raw:
and $|u'|$ unbounded at the end
where $r=0$ (at
$p_n^1$, a zero of $f_1$, $T_1=d^2b\ne0$; at $b_n$, a zero of $\beta_1$,
$T_2=s^2a\mathsf D\ne0$); at the other end $r=1$ and $|u'|\to\infty$ as
well, since $y$ has a simple zero there, unless $k=k_0$, where
$2nK=p_n^\alpha$, $y$ has a double zero at $2nK$ (as
$\alpha_1'(2nK)=(-1)^n4n^2E(K-E)\ne0$) and
$\sn(K-u)/\dn(K-u)=\sqrt{y/\mathsf D}$ (quarter-period shift), the root
taken with the sign of $p-2nK$, is analytic across $2nK$; hence so is the
continuation of $u$ from $B_n^-$ by $2K-u$ on $B_n^+$, which is what
Lemma~\ref{lem:crossing} requires at that end.
steps.note: The endpoint asymptotics, analytic continuation and finiteness argument have no compiled counterpart here. hL/hR remain explicit finite-tangency assumptions.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · apply crossing to each bracket
steps.raw:
So
Lemma~\ref{lem:crossing}, with \eqref{eq:zero-set}, applies to each bracket
separately: exactly one root on each closed bracket
steps.note: Lean m is article n − 1. JacobiFull and finite tangencies hL/hR remain assumptions; zero orders and identification of k₀ are not certified.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · simple roots and the double corner
steps.raw:
, simple off the
tangency phases, and simple at the corners as well, since $r=\sn^2u$ and
$1-r$ have the simple zeros just noted, except at the double corner $2nK$
for $k=k_0$.
steps.note: These zero-order claims have no corresponding compiled proof in the published snapshot.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · bracket roots exhaust the cell
steps.raw:
Since $p_n^1\in B_n^-$ and
$b_n<p_{n+1}^1$, these bracket roots exhaust the half-open cell.
steps.note: Set extensionality proves that the half-open cell zero set equals {p, q}, using the two bracket counts and the positive/negative exclusion branches.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · coincidence forces the common endpoint
steps.raw:
The roots on the
two closed brackets coincide only if both are the common endpoint
steps.note: The coincidence branch forces p = (2m+2)K; eL_eq_eR_iff proves contact iff K = 2E. This index does not identify the unique numerical k₀.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · identification of the critical modulus
steps.raw:
which
exists only for $k=k_0$
steps.note: The unique numerical k₀ and its identification with the elliptic equation K = 2E are not constructed in this Lean snapshot.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · location of coincident bracket roots
steps.raw: where it is the corner $(2nK,K)$ of both curves
steps.note: The coincidence branch proves p = (2m+2)K, with m = n − 1. This is a scalar location counterpart; the phase criterion is indexed in the next passage.

steps.title: 4.1 proof · phase at the common endpoint
steps.raw: met by the line exactly when $\psi\equiv K-2nK\equiv K$.
steps.note: The compiled equivalence characterizes J2(τ, 2nK) = 0 by τ = K + 2Kj. Along τ = ψ + 2nK this gives ψ ≡ K. Only this scalar phase criterion is indexed.
